title: A 40 km split assigns 44% of the Monte Cristo west centroid shift to changing event fractions on days 1-30 at M>=2.5
abstract: We tested whether distant events account for the west centroid shift in a fixed USGS Monte Cristo Range catalog. The sample has 331 events on days [1,7) and 305 on days [7,30), with preferred magnitude at least 2.5 within 100 km. The centroid shifts 4.737 km west. A symmetric split at 40 km assigns 2.074 km, or 43.79%, to changing event fractions and 2.662 km to changes within zones. The core-only shift is 2.539 km west, but its daily block-weight range includes zero. Boundaries of 25 and 30 km assign 67.68% and 61.58% to fractions. An ml-only check reduces the 40 km fraction term to 0.924 km. Thus, distance selection and magnitude types affect the assigned share. These are exact catalog summaries with conditional weight sensitivity ranges, not causal fractions or calibrated process intervals. One selected routine catalog, observation changes, exploratory choices and location error limit inference. We preserve the raw snapshot, source hashes, code, all draws, a figure, an independent audit and an offline repeat.

display.caption: The west centroid shift depends on distant events. Daily block-weight ranges leave the primary core shift uncertain. The 40 km mixture split is exact for this catalog.
